answer.decision: Choose tail-aware sampling that retains all error traces and requests above the p99 latency threshold while randomly sampling normal successful traffic at a lower rate.
answer.action: Deploy the validated prototype policy, preserving errors and p99-slow traces and configuring a nonzero random sample of normal traffic. Verify per-service latency-analysis coverage and at least a 40% realized cost reduction; tune the normal-traffic sampling rate or add per-service minimums if coverage is insufficient.
reasons: The prototype reduced stored trace volume by 55%, exceeding the 40% reduction requirement if stored volume is a suitable cost proxy.
The prototype retained all injected error and p99 test traces, matching the requirement to preserve errors and very slow requests.
Errors are only 0.7% of requests but provide 46% of traces used in incident reviews, making indiscriminate uniform or head-based sampling unsuitable.
More than 98% of volume is normal successful traffic, so sampling that category provides substantial savings while retaining high-value traces.
Independent full-aggregation metrics preserve broad service-level latency measurement, while sampled normal traces remain available for trace-level analysis.
The backend supports retention decisions after spans are assembled, making tail-aware sampling technically feasible.
assumptions: Stored-volume reduction translates sufficiently into billed-cost reduction.
The normal-traffic sample is nonzero and representative across services and relevant time windows.
The p99 classification is reliably calculated and applied.
The sampler has adequate buffering and operational capacity.
risks: Low-traffic services may have too few sampled normal traces unless per-service minimums or stratification are used.
A global p99 threshold may miss requests that are unusually slow for a particular service.
Tail sampling introduces buffering, memory use, decision latency, and operational complexity.
Overload, incomplete traces, or classification failures could weaken retention guarantees.
Actual bill reduction may be below 55% if significant ingestion or processing costs occur before retention decisions.

citations.claim: The prototype reduced stored trace volume by 55% while retaining all injected error and p99 test traces.
Errors comprise 0.7% of requests but account for 46% of traces used during incident reviews.
Requests above the p99 latency threshold represent 1% of volume.
Normal successful traffic represents more than 98% of trace volume.
Metrics are independently collected at full aggregation and do not require retaining every trace.
The backend supports different retention rules after spans are assembled, enabling tail-based decisions before storage.
